title: Release lorax 0.2.0
description:
Prepare for release:

* [x] `git pull`
* [x] Check [current CRAN check results](https://cran.rstudio.org/web/checks/check_results_lorax.html)
* [x] [Polish NEWS](https://style.tidyverse.org/news.html#news-release)
* [x] `urlchecker::url_check()`
* [x] `devtools::build_readme()`
* [x] `devtools::check(remote = TRUE, manual = TRUE)`
* [x] `devtools::check_win_devel()`
* [ ] Update `cran-comments.md`
* [ ] `git push`
* [ ] Draft blog post

Submit to CRAN:

* [ ] `usethis::use_version('minor')`
* [ ] `devtools::submit_cran()`
* [ ] Approve email

Wait for CRAN...

* [x] Accepted :tada:
* [ ] Finish & publish blog post
* [ ] Add link to blog post in pkgdown news menu
* [x] `usethis::use_github_release()`
* [x] `usethis::use_dev_version(push = TRUE)`
* [ ] Share on social media
* [ ] Slack link to blog post, bluesky, and linkedin in #open-source-comms

title: README.Rmd has placeholder text and no rendered README.md
description:
Landed on the repo and noticed two things:

1. The README still has the default usethis skeleton — 
   "The goal of lorax is to ..." and 
   "FILL THIS IN! HOW CAN PEOPLE INSTALL YOUR DEV PACKAGE?" 
   are still there.

2. There's a README.Rmd but no README.md — GitHub renders 
   the raw Rmd source instead of the knitted output, so the 
   code chunks show as plain text rather than running.

Even a one-liner about what the package does and a 
`pak::pak("topepo/lorax")` install line would help anyone 
stumbling across it.

Happy to leave this open as a reminder or close it if 
you're still in early development. Also happy to help with 
tests, documentation, or anything else if useful.

title: catboost: segfault when decoding CTR splits from a model trained with final_ctr_computation_mode = "Skip"
description:
When a catboost model is trained with `final_ctr_computation_mode = "Skip"`, the CTR tables are not saved in the model, but the trees can still contain `OnlineCtr` splits. `extract_rules()` (via `cb_decode_ctrs()` → `cb_probe_leaves()`) writes a probe model from the model JSON, which has no `ctr_data`, and `catboost.predict()` on that probe model segfaults. This takes down the R session (or a parallel worker, which shows up in tune as an unrelated `bind_rows()` error).

``` r
library(catboost)
library(lorax)

dat <- modeldata::deliveries[1:900, ]
x <- as.data.frame(dat[, -1])

fit_ctb <- function(mode) {
  pool <- catboost.load_pool(x, label = dat$time_to_delivery)
  catboost.train(
    pool,
    params = list(
      iterations = 25,
      depth = 2,
      learning_rate = 0.07,
      random_seed = 2964,
      logging_level = "Silent",
      allow_writing_files = FALSE,
      final_ctr_computation_mode = mode
    )
  )
}

# works: 99 rules
nrow(extract_rules(fit_ctb("Default"), tree = 1:25, data = x))

# crashes R
extract_rules(fit_ctb("Skip"), tree = 1:25, data = x)
#>  *** caught segfault ***
#> address 0x0, cause 'invalid permissions'
#>
#> Traceback:
#>  1: predict.catboost.Model(model, pool, ...)
#>  2: catboost::catboost.predict(model = probe_model, pool = pool, prediction_type = "RawFormulaVal")
#>  3: rlang::eval_bare(cl)
#>  4: cb_probe_leaves(json, lapply(info[chunk], function(i) i$split), do.call(rbind, probes))
#>  5: cb_decode_ctrs(json, tree_num, features, pred_data)
#>  ...
#>  8: extract_rules.catboost.Model(...)
```

`day` has 7 levels, which is more than `one_hot_max_size`, so catboost uses CTR splits for it. `as.party()` also calls `cb_decode_ctrs()`, so it should have the same problem.

**Suggested fix:** before building the probe model, check that the model JSON has `ctr_data` when any split has `split_type == "OnlineCtr"`, and raise an informative error if it doesn't (e.g., that the model was trained with `final_ctr_computation_mode = "Skip"` and the CTR splits can't be converted to rules).

Versions: R 4.5.2, lorax 0.1.0.9000 (2dcd015), catboost 1.2.10.
